context: Create a dedicated artifact boundary that opens a trusted central root once and resolves relative components beneath its directory descriptor with no-follow checks. Validate bounded result envelopes, record a canonical digest, and persist a disposition for every artifact. Decision gate: stop if containment relies on string-prefix or pre-open realpath checks, if a result can be replayed across runs, or if closeout can succeed with an artifact still only in a removable worktree.
description: Ensure worker result envelopes and every declared artifact survive linked-worktree retirement. A successful turn must bind to the exact registry, task, run, turn, prompt digest, and accepted head, and each artifact must be secured by an accepted commit or copied into a central bounded artifact root before cleanup can proceed.

anti_patterns.dont: Call a plain SHA digest cryptographic authentication
anti_patterns.instead: Describe it as integrity and correlation unless a separate signing model is approved
anti_patterns.why: A worker that knows the fields can recompute it

anti_patterns.dont: Treat a central result envelope as proof that its declared artifacts are durable
anti_patterns.instead: Record an accepted-commit or central-copy disposition for every artifact
anti_patterns.why: Artifacts may still reside only in the worker worktree

anti_patterns.instead: Resolve by construction beneath a trusted open root descriptor
anti_patterns.why: It permits prefix mistakes and leaves a time-of-check to time-of-use race

preserves.behavior: A digest detects accidental or replayed mismatch but is not described as authentication without a signing trust model.
Artifact paths stored in the registry are central-root-relative and never depend on a worker cwd.
No worker-controlled symlink or path component can redirect central ingestion.
Successful result files remain bounded to the existing maximum unless an approved contract changes it.
